{"documentId": "f_a37b403d5200d4f0a31d31", "title": "Stockholder close-out notes", "name": "Stockholder close-out notes", "revisionId": "3c986c6ce3", "createdTime": "2026-02-13T01:05:41Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-13T01:05:41Z", "text": "Stockholder close-out notes

These replace my earlier outreach notes.

What needs doing
- the reach-out I promised to the investors, one by one, not one mail to everyone
- where I left things today in #winddown: the angels are what's open from my list, besides the Sunset onboarding
- the investor email on the Task List: take my draft from #winddown and bring it up to date as a letter I can send. the update outline has the sections
- the holder sheet comes first, the notes and everything else run off it. Finish my draft one in the folder rather than starting another. Share it and the letter with Robert
- notes ready for me by Tuesday, as Gmail drafts. I said I'd archive google after the 15th but that waits, we keep it until the data is extracted, so my drafts are safe until I've gone through them. I read and send each note myself
- everything goes in the close-out folder, not the Wind Down one, that one is the vendor and termination papers
- Griffin's partner gets a heads-up as a reply to all on their own Board position mail from Feb 12, asking for their vote as preferred holders on the dissolution. That one can go out once the sheet is done
- when the sheet is ready, reply under my list in #winddown and say who goes first

How each holder gets handled
- Carta is the record, over any date in the letters. If a line's last day has passed, it holds nothing.
- One row per issue on the sheet, and the counts go by rows. At most one note per person. The three of us get no row, only the totals.
- Told means a written message about the closing, sent to them directly and delivered, from one of the three of us (a post in a channel doesn't count); for a fund, its partner.
- Everyone still holding something gets what they are owed: the closing if they have not been told, their last day if they have one. Whoever's last day comes first goes first.
- Each note says what they hold.
- Anything they asked about their holding that we never answered gets answered in their note, if they get one.
- Messages go to the email on each holder's issue.

Labels for the sheet: Nothing, Already told, Closing, Last day, Closing and last day.
"}

Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.
• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets, and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company.

content.content: {"result":"[{\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Daily aggregated user metrics per game and platform. Includes DAU, new/returning split, session counts, average session length, and D1/D7/D30 retention percentages. combo_fighter from 2025-12-27, domino_delights from 2023-11-01. Zombie Match 3D is ABSENT BY DESIGN and its absence is a fact about the company, not a gap: it never had a DAU instrument. Derive ZM3D volume from ANALYTICS.MARKETING.INSTALL_EVENTS and ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.USER_COHORT_RETENTION instead. Do not synthesise a ZM3D DAU series. Aggregated upstream of the retained event tables. RAW_GAME_EVENTS and STG_EVENTS_ENRICHED retain a 1:8 session sample, and PROGRESSION_EVENTS, SESSION_LEVEL_EVENTS and AD_IMPRESSION_EVENTS a 1:16 sample, so a recount from those tables will not match these totals.\", \"row_count\": 1682, \"created_at\": \"2023-10-28T00:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_METRICS_AGG\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DAILY_METRICS_AGG\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Daily metrics mart derived from the DAU and revenue tables. Aggregated upstream of the retained event tables. RAW_GAME_EVENTS and STG_EVENTS_ENRICHED retain a 1:8 session sample, and PROGRESSION_EVENTS, SESSION_LEVEL_EVENTS and AD_IMPRESSION_EVENTS a 1:16 sample, so a recount from those tables will not match these totals.\", \"row_count\": 1682, \"created_at\": \"2023-10-28T00:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_METRICS_AGG\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_COUNTRY\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DIM_COUNTRY\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Country dimension distinguishing revenue countries from UA-only countries.\", \"row_count\": 10, \"created_at\": \"2023-10-28T00:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_COUNTRY\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_DATE\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DIM_DATE\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Calendar dimension over the active warehouse period.\", \"row_count\": 1026, \"created_at\": \"2023-04-24T00:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_DATE\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_DEVICE\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DIM_DEVICE\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Device dimension: the phone/tablet models seen across HG4 titles with platform, OS version, form factor, and an estimated market value. Anchored to the device deep-dive device space (iPhone/iPad + Samsung/Pixel/Oppo/OnePlus). Domino Delights install sample skews ~77% iOS.\", \"row_count\": 17, \"created_at\": \"2023-10-28T00:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_DEVICE\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_PLAYER\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DIM_PLAYER\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Player dimension for the install universe, 31,210 rows. Acquisition channels are derived from INSTALL_EVENTS and match AD_SPEND_DAILY. Channel mix: adjoe 8,730, applovin 699, google_uac 256, meta 1,455, organic 15,610, unity_ads 4,460.\", \"row_count\": 31210, \"created_at\": \"2023-10-28T00:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_PLAYER\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.LEVEL_PERFORMANCE\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"LEVEL_PERFORMANCE\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Per-level aggregates, 5,497 rows. Level ranges present: combo_fighter 1-442, domino_delights 1-4755, zombie_match_3d 1-300. fail_reason_top is the modal failure for that level and uses each title's OWN fail vocabulary -- the three games do not share one. Aggregated upstream of the retained event tables. RAW_GAME_EVENTS and STG_EVENTS_ENRICHED retain a 1:8 session sample, and PROGRESSION_EVENTS, SESSION_LEVEL_EVENTS and AD_IMPRESSION_EVENTS a 1:16 sample, so a recount from those tables will not match these totals.\", \"row_count\": 5497, \"created_at\": \"2023-10-28T00:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.LEVEL_PERFORMANCE\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.PLAYER_DAILY_PROGRESS\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"PLAYER_DAILY_PROGRESS\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Per-player daily snapshot: level reached, sessions, coins, boosters, levels attempted/completed, purchase flag. coins_earned is what play paid out; coins bought from the store arrive as iap_grant rows in RESOURCE_FLOW_EVENTS and are not counted here. coins_spent and boosters_used count purchases at each game's shipped booster prices, so a player-day with no affordable purchase reads zero, and boosters_used is zero throughout for Combo Fighter, which ships none. made_purchase is reconciled against IAP_TRANSACTIONS at the game-date grain. Holds 183,033 player-days over 31,210 distinct players, against 31,210 installs lifetime -- a player appears here only on days they actually played. Aggregated upstream of the retained event tables. RAW_GAME_EVENTS and STG_EVENTS_ENRICHED retain a 1:8 session sample, and PROGRESSION_EVENTS, SESSION_LEVEL_EVENTS and AD_IMPRESSION_EVENTS a 1:16 sample, so a recount from those tables will not match these totals.\", \"row_count\": 183033, \"created_at\": \"2023-10-28T00:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.PLAYER_DAILY_PROGRESS\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.SESSION_LEVEL_EVENTS\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"SESSION_LEVEL_EVENTS\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Derived from RAW_EVENTS and retained at a 1:16 session sample; sampling is by session, so every event of a retained session is present. Raw level attempt events (sampled). Each row = one player action: level_started, level_completed, level_failed, booster_used, or tutorial_step. HARMONY GAMES                          : Reset Financing Framework

(Discussion Only)
Purpose​
We are proposing a reset financing to (1) simplify the cap table and governance, (2) create room
for a refreshed team equity plan, and (3) align ongoing ownership with ongoing support via a
pay-to-play structure.

Round economics

      ●​ Instrument: priced preferred equity (new series)
      ●​ Pre-money valuation: $2.25M
      ●​ New money: up to $250K total (includes $50K founders      )
      ●​ Post-money: $2.5M
      ●​ New issuance: investors in this round collectively receive 10% post-money fully
         diluted
      ●​ Employee equity: establish a 10% post-money option pool (set aside at closing)​


Cap                   table reset principles



      ●​
           founders
                  : founders
                                   ? common is preserved.

      ●​ Legacy investors: legacy investor holdings will be recapitalized into a smaller
         common position as part of the reset, so the cap table reflects current-stage
         economics.
      ●​ Governance reset: legacy investor rights are replaced with a clean, standard set of
         documents for the new round.​


Pay-to-play (alignment mechanism)

      ●​ Legacy investors may participate in the new round on the same terms as new investors.
      ●​ Participation is expected to be pay-to-play, meaning ongoing investor rights and future
         participation rights are tied to participating in this reset round.​

content.content:
Hi Leonard,

Quick one from legal for the intake. Before they start on the stockholder side they'll need this from you, ideally in one sheet:

- One line per holder of stock or options, with what each holds today (for options, what's vested) and any last day
- Total shares and options outstanding
- A count of holders by what each still needs to hear from you
- Directors in office, and who holds the preferred vote

Formal notices are a separate step that legal will walk you through later, so your own notes to holders don't need to double as notices.

content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_d690045a2f2bf47108ae99\", \"title\": \"Harmony Games Inc Disclosure Schedule.docx\", \"name\": \"Harmony Games Inc Disclosure Schedule.docx\", \"revisionId\": \"a0bb10c869\", \"createdTime\": \"2023-07-07T13:18:10Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2023-07-10T16:51:03Z\", \"text\": \"DISCLOSURE SCHEDULE Section 1 - Representations and Warranties of the Company\\n1.1 Organization, Good Standing, corporate Power and Qualification\\nThe Company is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware.\\nThe Company has all requisite corporate power and authority to carry on its current business and proposed activities.\\nThe Company is duly qualified to transact business and is in good standing in all jurisdictions where failure to qualify would have a Material Adverse Effect.\\n1.2 Capitalization\\n(a) Authorized Capital: - 10,000,000 shares of Common Stock, $0.0001 par value per share, 6,000,000 of which are issued and outstanding. - 3,051,882 shares of Preferred Stock, none of which are issued and outstanding. 3,051,882 shares have been designated as Series Seed Preferred Stock.\\n(b) Reserved Shares: - The Company has reserved 1,017,294 shares of Common Stock for issuance under the Stock Plan. - [_______] shares of Common Stock have been issued pursuant to restricted stock purchase agreements. - Options to purchase [_______] shares of Common Stock have been granted and are currently outstanding. - [__________] shares of Common Stock remain available for issuance under the Stock Plan. - The Stock Plan and forms of agreements used thereunder have been provided to the Purchasers.\\n(c) Capitalization Details: - Section 2.2(c) of the Disclosure Schedule provides a detailed breakdown of the Company's capitalization, including issued and outstanding Common Stock, outstanding stock options, shares of Common Stock reserved for future award grants under the Stock Plan, each series of Preferred Stock, and warrants or stock purchase rights. - Except for certain exceptions mentioned, There are no outstanding options, warrants, rights, or agreements to purchase or acquire shares of Common Stock or Preferred Stock. - All outstanding shares of Common Stock and underlying options are subject to a right of first r[USERNAME_4303] and a lock-up or market standoff agreement of not less than 180 days following the Company's initial public offering.\\n(d) Stock Agreements: - None of the Company's stock purchase agreements or stock option documents contain provisions for acceleration of vesting or other changes in vesting provisions or terms. - The Company has not adjusted or amended the exercise price of any previously awarded stock options. - The Company has no obligation (contingent or otherwise) to purchase or redeem any of its capital stock.\\n(e) Section 409A: - The Company believes that any \\\"nonqualified deferred compensation plan\\\" (as defined under Section 409A(d)(1) of the Code) complies with Section 409A in form and operation. - No payment under any 409A Plan is or will be subject to penalties under Section 409A(a)(1) of the Code.\\n(f) Waivers: - No other parties have rights to purchase any of the Shares covered by this Agreement.\\n1.3 Subsidiaries\\nThe Company does not own or control any interest in any other corporation, partnership, trust, joint venture, limited liability company, association, or business entity.\\nThe Company is not a participant in any joint venture, partnership, or similar arrangement.\\n1.4 Authorization\\nAll necessary corporate actions required by the Company's Board of Directors and stockholders to authorize the Transaction Agreements and the issuance of Shares have been taken.\\nAll necessary actions by the Company's officers for the execution, delivery, performance, and issuance of the Transaction Agreements and Shares have been taken.\\nThe Transaction Agreements, when executed and delivered by the Company, constitute valid and legally binding obligations enforceable in accordance with their terms, subject to certain limitations.\\n1.5 Valid Issuance of Shares\\nThe Shares, when issued, sold, and delivered in accordance with the terms of the Agreement, will be validly issued, fully paid, nonassessable, and free of transfer restrictions except those under the Transaction Agreements, applicable securities laws, and liens or encumbrances imposed by a Purchaser.\\nAssuming the accuracy of the representations of the Purchasers and subject to filings described in the Voting Agreement, the issuance of Shares complies with applicable federal and state securities laws.\\nThe Common Stock issuable upon conversion of the Shares has been duly reserved and, upon issuance according to the Restated Certificate, will be validly issued, fully paid, nonassessable, and free of transfer restrictions except those under the Transaction Agreements, applicable securities laws, and liens or encumbrances imposed by a Purchaser.\\nAssuming the accuracy of the representations of the Purchasers and the Voting Agreement, the issuance of Common Stock upon conversion of the Shares complies with applicable federal and state securities laws.\\n1.6 Governmental Consents and Filings\\nNo consent, approval, order, or authorization of any federal, state, or local governmental authority is required by the Company for the completion of the transactions contemplated by the Agreement, except for filings under applicable securities laws.\\n1.7 Litigation\\nThere are no pending claims, actions, suits, proceedings, or investigations against the Company, its officers, directors, or Key Employees that question the validity of the Transaction Agreements or the Company's right to enter into them or consummate the transactions.\\nThe Company, its officers, directors, and Key Employees are not subject to any orders, writs, injunctions, judgments, or decrees of any court or government agency that would affect the Company.\\nThere are no pending actions, suits, proceedings, or investigations initiated or intended to be initiated by the Company.\\nThe Company has disclosed any known actions, suits, proceedings, or investigations involving the prior employment of its employees, services provided, proprietary information, or obligations under agreements with prior employers.\\n1.8 Intellectual Property\\n(a) Ownership and Rights: - The Company owns or possesses sufficient legal rights to all Company Intellectual Property without conflicting with or infringing on the rights of others. - The Company has not received any communications alleging infringement of Intellectual Property of any other person.\\n(b) Violations and Infringements: - No product or service marketed or sold by the Company violates any license or infringes on the Intellectual Property rights of any other person.\\n(c) Options, Licenses, and Agreements: - There are no outstanding options, licenses, agreements, claims, encumbrances, or shared ownership interests related to Company Intellectual Property. - The Company is not bound by any options, licenses, or agreements regarding the Intellectual Property of any other person.\\n(d) Software Programs: - The Company possesses valid licenses for all software programs used on its computers and other software-enabled electronic devices.\\n(e) Assignment of Intellectual Property: - Employees and consultants have assigned all Intellectual Property developed during their employment or consulting relationship with the Company to the Company. - No inventions or Intellectual Property of employees or consultants prior to their employment by the Company are necessary for the Company's operations.\\n(f) Patents, Trademarks, Copyrights, and Domain Names: - Section 2.8(f) of the Disclosure Schedule provides a list of all owned or purportedly owned patents, trademarks, service marks, tradenames, copyrights, domain names, and licenses related to the Company's Intellectual Property.\\n(g) Open Source Software: - The Company has not used or distributed any Open Source Software in a manner that materially restricts its proprietary interests in its products or services. - Schedule 2.8(g) of the Disclosure Schedule lists all Open Source Software utilized by the Company.\\n(h) Government Funding: - No government funding, facilities, or funding from third parties were used in the development of Company Intellectual Property. - Persons involved in the creation or development of Company Intellectual Property have not performed services for government entities or educational institutions that would affect the Company's rights.\\n1.9 Compliance with Other Instruments\\nThe Company is not in violation or default of any provisions of its Restated Certificate or Bylaws.\\nThe Company is not in violation or default under any instrument, judgment, order, writ, decree, lease, agreement, contract, or purchase order that is required to be listed on the Disclosure Schedule.\\nThe Company is not in violation of any federal or state statute, rule, or regulation that would have a Material Adverse Effect.\\nThe execution, delivery, and performance of the Transaction Agreements and the transactions contemplated therein will not result in any violation, default, conflict, or creation of liens, charges, or encumbrances upon the Company's assets or the suspension, revocation, forfeiture, or nonrenewal of any material permit or license applicable to the Company.\\n1.10 Agreements; Actions\\n(a) Agreements: - Other than the Transaction Agreements, There are no agreements, instruments, contracts, or proposed transactions exceeding $25,000 that involve the Company's obligations or payments. - There are no agreements limiting the Company's exclusive rights or involving indemnification for infringements of proprietary rights.\\n(b) Actions: - The Company has not declared or paid dividends, authorized or made distributions, incurred indebtedness exceeding $25,000 individually or $50,000 in aggregate (except fully satisfied or discharged indebtedness), made loans or advances (except ordinary business advances), or disposed of assets other than in the ordinary course of business. - For the purpose of aggregation, indebtedness, liabilities, agreements, and transactions involving the same persons or affiliated persons are considered.\\n(c) Guarantees: - The Company is not a guarantor or indemnitor of any indebtedness of any other person.\\n1.11 Certain Transactions\\n(a) Officer, Director, and Consultant Agreements: - Except for standard employee benefits, offer letters, Confidential (f) Patents, Trademarks, Copyrights, and Domain Names: - Section 2.8(f) of the Disclosure Schedule provides a list of all owned or purportedly owned patents, trademarks, service marks, tradenames, copyrights, domain names, and licenses related to the Company's Intellectual Property.
(g) Open Source Software: - The Company has not used or distributed any Open Source Software in a manner that materially restricts its proprietary interests in its products or services. - Schedule 2.8(g) of the Disclosure Schedule lists all Open Source Software utilized by the Company.
(h) Government Funding: - No government funding, facilities, or funding from third parties were used in the development of Company Intellectual Property. - Persons involved in the creation or development of Company Intellectual Property have not performed services for government entities or educational institutions that would affect the Company's rights.
1.9 Compliance with Other Instruments
The Company is not in violation or default of any provisions of its Restated Certificate or Bylaws.
The Company is not in violation or default under any instrument, judgment, order, writ, decree, lease, agreement, contract, or purchase order that is required to be listed on the Disclosure Schedule.
The Company is not in violation of any federal or state statute, rule, or regulation that would have a Material Adverse Effect.
The execution, delivery, and performance of the Transaction Agreements and the transactions contemplated therein will not result in any violation, default, conflict, or creation of liens, charges, or encumbrances upon the Company's assets or the suspension, revocation, forfeiture, or nonrenewal of any material permit or license applicable to the Company.
1.10 Agreements; Actions
(a) Agreements: - Other than the Transaction Agreements, There are no agreements, instruments, contracts, or proposed transactions exceeding $25,000 that involve the Company's obligations or payments. - There are no agreements limiting the Company's exclusive rights or involving indemnification for infringements of proprietary rights.
(b) Actions: - The Company has not declared or paid dividends, authorized or made distributions, incurred indebtedness exceeding $25,000 individually or $50,000 in aggregate (except fully satisfied or discharged indebtedness), made loans or advances (except ordinary business advances), or disposed of assets other than in the ordinary course of business. - For the purpose of aggregation, indebtedness, liabilities, agreements, and transactions involving the same persons or affiliated persons are considered.
(c) Guarantees: - The Company is not a guarantor or indemnitor of any indebtedness of any other person.
1.11 Certain Transactions
(a) Officer, Director, and Consultant Agreements: - Except for standard employee benefits, offer letters, Confidential Information Agreements, director/officer indemnification agreements, and the Transaction Agreements, There are no agreements, understandings, or proposed transactions between the Company and its officers, directors, consultants, Key Employees, or any affiliates.
(b) Indebtedness: - The Company is not directly or indirectly indebted to its directors, officers, employees, their spouses, children, or any affiliates, except for ordinary business expenses, advances, employee relocation expenses, and customary employee benefits. - No directors, officers, employees, immediate family members, or affiliates are indebted to the Company.
1.12 Rights of Registration and Voting Rights
Except as provided in the Investors' Rights Agreement, the Company is not obligated to register any of its currently outstanding securities under the Securities Act.
To the Company's knowledge, no stockholder has entered into agreements regarding the voting of the Company's capital shares, except as contemplated in the Voting Agreement.
1.13 Property
The Company's owned property and assets are free and clear of mortgages, liens, loans, and encumbrances, except for statutory liens for current taxes and ordinary course liens that do not materially impair ownership or use.
With respect to leased property, the Company is in compliance with leases and holds valid leasehold interests free of liens, claims, or encumbrances other than those of the lessors.
The Company does not own any real property.
1.14 Material Liabilities
The Company has no liability or obligation, absolute or contingent, except for obligations incurred after the date of incorporation not exceeding $100,000 in aggregate and obligations under contracts made in the ordinary course of business not required to be reflected in financial statements prepared according to GAAP
1.15 Changes
Since the Company's date of incorporation, There have been no changes in assets, liabilities, financial condition, or operating results that would have a Material Adverse Effect, except for changes in the ordinary course of business.
There have been no significant damages, destructions, or losses.
The Company has not waived or compromised any valuable rights or material debts owed to it.
There have been no satisfaction or discharge of liens, claims, or encumbrances, except in the ordinary course of business.
There have been no material changes to material contracts or agreements.
The officers will be compensated with a salary of $125,000 per year.
There have been no resignations or terminations of employment of officers or Key Employees.
The Company has not created any significant mortgages, pledges, security interests, or liens on its material properties or assets, except for certain statutory liens and ordinary course liens that do not materially impair ownership or use.
The Company has not made any significant loans or guarantees to employees, officers, directors, or their immediate families, except for travel advances and ordinary business advances.
There have been no dividends, distributions, redemptions, purchases, or other acquisitions of the Company's capital stock, except as contemplated in the Transaction Agreements.
There have been no sales, assignments, or transfers of any Company Intellectual Property that could reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect.
The Company has not received notice of loss or material order cancellations by any major customer.
Except for events affecting the economy or the Company's industry generally, There have been no other events or conditions that could reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect.
The Company has not committed to any of the described actions in this section.
1.16 Employee Matters
(a) Contracts and Interference: - None of the Company's employees are obligated under contracts or agreements that would materially interfere with their ability to promote the Company's interests or conflict with the Company's business. - The execution, delivery, and carrying on of the Company's business, including the Transaction Agreements, do not conflict with or result in a breach of any contracts, covenants, or instruments to which the employees are obligated.
(b) Payment and Compliance: - The Company is not delinquent in payments to employees, consultants, or independent contractors for wages, salaries, commissions, or other direct compensation. - The Company has complied with applicable state and federal equal employment opportunity laws and other employment-related laws, including those related to wages, hours, worker classification, and collective bargaining. - The Company has withheld and paid all amounts required to be withheld from employees, and it is not liable for any arrears of wages, taxes, penalties, or other sums for non-compliance.
(c) Employee Terminations and Severance: - To the Company's knowledge, no Key Employee intends to terminate employment or become unavailable. - The Company has no present intention to terminate the employment of Key Employees. - Employment of each employee is terminable at the Company's will. - Except as set forth in Section 2.16(c)(i) of the Disclosure Schedule or required by law, no severance or other payments become due upon termination. - The Company has no policy, practice, plan, or program of paying severance compensation except as specified in Section 2.16(c)(ii) of the Disclosure Schedule.
(d) Equity Incentives: - The Company has not made any inconsistent representations regarding equity incentives to officers, employees, directors, or consultants.
(e) Former Key Employees: - Each former Key Employee has entered into an agreement releasing claims against the Company arising from their employment.
(f) Employee Benefit Plans: - Section 2.16(f) of the Disclosure Schedule lists each employee benefit plan subject to ERISA, including the Company's contributions and compliance with applicable laws.
1.17 Tax Returns and Payments
There are no federal, state, county, local, or foreign income or other material taxes due and payable by the Company that have not been timely paid.
There are no accrued and unpaid federal, state, county, local, or foreign income or other material taxes, unless being contested in good faith with adequate reserves established in accordance with GAAP.
There have been no examinations or audits of tax returns by any applicable governmental agency.
The Company has duly and timely filed all required federal, state, county, local, and foreign income or other material tax returns, and There are no waivers of applicable statutes of limitations.
1.18 Insurance
The Company has insurance policies in full force and effect, with extended coverage, sufficient in amount (subject to reasonable deductions) to replace any damaged or destroyed properties.
1.19 Employee Agreements
Each current and former employee, consultant, and officer of the Company has executed a Confidential Information Agreement with the Company.
No Key Employee is known to be in violation of any agreement described in this section.
1.20 Permits
The Company holds all necessary franchises, permits, licenses, and similar authorities for its business operations.
The Company is not in material default under any such franchises, permits, licenses, or authorities.
1.21 corporate Documents
The Certificate of Incorporation and Bylaws of the Company are in the form provided to the Purchasers.
The provided minute books accurately reflect all actions by the directors and stockholders since the date of incorporation.
1.22 83(b) Elections
To the Company's knowledge, all eligible individuals who acquired unvested shares of the Company's Common Stock have timely filed or will timely file elections and notices under Section 83(b) of the Code.
1.23 Qualified Small Business Stock
As of the Initial Closing, the Company meets the criteria as an eligible corporation under Section 1202(e)(4) of the Code.
The Company has not made purchases of its own stock described in Code Section 1202(c)(3)(B) during the one-year period preceding the Initial Closing, except for disregarded purchases under Treasury Regulation Section 1.1202-2.
The Company's aggregate gross assets, as defined by Code Section 1202(d)(2), have not exceeded $50 million at any time between incorporation and the Initial Closing, taking into account aggregated assets of related corporations as required by Code Section 1202(d)(3).
1.24 Privacy and Cybersecurity
The Company is and has been in compliance with applicable laws and Privacy Requirements regarding the collection, storage, use, and disclosure of Personal Information.
The Company maintains reasonable physical, technical, and administrative security measures to protect Personal Information.
There have been no unlawful, unauthorized, or significant access, use, modification, acquisition, or disclosure of Personal Information or unauthorized access to confidential information or trade secrets.
1.25 Disclosure
The Company has provided all requested information to the Purchasers for their decision to acquire the Shares, including the Business Plan.
No representation or warranty of the Company contains any untrue statement of material fact or omits a material fact necessary to make the statements not misleading.
The Business Plan was prepared in good faith, but the Company does not guarantee achieving projected results.
The Company has not delivered a private placement memorandum or similar document or written disclosure typically furnished to purchasers of securities.

Harmony Games Inc. is shutting down and preparing to file for dissolution.\\nBecause of this, we need to terminate our agreement with Singular effective immediately. Unfortunately, the company is insolvent and we have no cash reserves left, There are no funds available to pay any remaining balance.\\nWe have valued the relationship and the team at Singular. We have not come close to using the plan, we have spent well under 1% of our ad spend cap, and we would appreciate your help in making this a clean, mutual early termination so we can properly close down without leaving obligations on your books.\\nPlease confirm in writing that the contract and any related renewals are cancelled as of today, and let us know what you need from us to close the account and stop any further charges. If helpful, we can provide the stamp-certified Certificate of Dissolution once filed to support your internal closeout.\\nThank you,\\n Leonard Hayes\", \"channel\": \"C0ADGSZKR3R\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770932147.282819\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"<@EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID> note for Unity team\\n\\nHi Unity Team,\\nWe have unfortunate news. Our company, Harmony Games is shutting down and preparing to file for dissolution.\\n\\nBecause of this, we are terminating our Unity Pro licensing agreement effective immediately. Unfortunately, the company is insolvent and we have no cash reserves left, There are no funds available to pay any remaining balance. We are filing for the Certificate of Dissolution once we resolve this one last item, as we\\u2019re working with existing vendors to properly shut down without any obligations on their books.\\n\\nPlease confirm in writing that the contract and any related renewals are cancelled as of today, and let us know what you need from us to close the account and stop any further charges. If helpful, we can provide the stamp-certified Certificate of Dissolution once filed to support your internal closeout.\\n\\nThank you,\\nArthur Blake\", \"channel\": \"C0ADGSZKR3R\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770859981.856189\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I\\u2019m hoping the data will cover our cost of shutting down orderly at least\", \"channel\": \"C0ADGSZKR3R\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770839984.194409\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"<!here> per our conversation we\\u2019ll be shutting down the company. I\\u2019ll archive everyone\\u2019s Google Account\\u2019s by Feb 15 - please save all your personal files / emails etc. on your local before you lose access. Same goes for Slack and other accounts\", \"channel\": \"C05KNDCHAAG\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770838529.954559\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"let\\u2019s then give them a chance to tell us how much would it cost to properly shut down\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770838470.719169\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Hi Leonard\\n\\nI\\u2019m sorry to hear that. Given your financial situation we\\u2019re happy to remove that bill and discount 100% the time we\\u2019ve spent reviewing the documents. Our goal here is always to make sure we do right by our client and we don\\u2019t want to pursue a client that has run out of funds before much work has been done.\\n\\nIf you\\u2019d like to discuss an arrangement to shut down the entity let us know. We can provide you with a fixed fee. If not, no worries and we wish you the best of luck going forward.\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770836625.652859\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Hi [PERSON_NAME_17634],\\n\\nUnfortunately, we are unable to move forward with the fundraising plan as originally discussed. The company has completely run out of funds and we are shutting it down.\\n\\nWe would like to settle for the work performed to date, but our current financial situation is extremely limited. We were not aware that the exploratory call would be a billable expense; had we known, we would not have proceeded with it yet alone let you guys explore the governing docs.\\n\\nIf you would like to jump on a quick call to discuss how we can resolve this, please let me know.\\n\\nBest regards,\\n\\nLeonard Hayes\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770832312.713589\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"<@EMPLOYEE_0024_SLACK_ID> we are shutting down Harmony Games unfortunately and last month\\u2019s payment was our last payment\", \"channel\": \"C05URGU759U\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770827028.233669\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I\\u2019m gonna share the shut down news with the team today\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770824780.548099\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"There is a chance but I was gonna make the announcement today that we will be shutting down harmonygames. We started the process and won't be able to pay anyone in February. In fact my plan is to send\\nEveryone official termination letters as early as today. I will address all questions today at the prototype meeting. \", \"channel\": \"D05Q3QAH2QZ\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770769746.793879\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"If your *Q4 payroll was basically zero*, that does *not* automatically mean \\u201czero R&D credit\\u201d, but it _does_ make it more likely you see *no immediate cash benefit*, depending on what you mean by \\u201cget anything.\\u201d\\nWhat the R&D credit is based on\\nThe federal R&D credit is calculated *for the tax year*, not by quarter, using *Qualified Research Expenses (QREs)*, which commonly include:\\n\\u2022 *W-2 wages* for employees doing qualified R&D work\\n\\u2022 *Supplies* used in qualified research\\n\\u2022 *Contract research* (generally *65%* of eligible amounts) \\nSo \\u201cQ4 payroll was zero\\u201d only reduces the credit if it means your *annual* qualified wages were low. If you had meaningful qualified payroll in Q1 to Q3, it still counts for the year.\\nWhy you may \\u201cget nothing\\u201d even if you have a credit\\nThe credit generally reduces *tax you owe*. If you owe *no federal income tax*, the credit may not produce a refund, it usually becomes a carryforward. The IRS describes the credit as computed on Form 6765.\\nFor many businesses, unused general business credits can be carried forward (commonly up to *20 years*).\\nThe startup payroll tax offset (only matters if you have payroll tax)\\nIf you qualified and made the election, you can apply some of the R&D credit against *employer payroll taxes*, but it is limited to the employer share of *social Security* (and, since 2023, potentially *Medicare* for any remaining amount).\\nKey implication for your question:\\nIf your *Q4 payroll taxes were near zero*, you likely could not use much credit *in that quarter*.\\nUnused payroll-offset credit can *carry forward to later quarters*, but only helps if you have future payroll tax liability.\\n\\u2022 You must elect it properly on *Form 6765*, and then apply it on payroll filings using *Form 8974*. \\nPractical answer for \\u201cwe spent $4K, did we get nothing?\\u201d\\nYou \\u201cget nothing\\u201d in the real-world sense if all of the below are true:\\n1. *Very low annual QREs* (for you this is often wages, but could include contractor R&D)\\n2. *No federal income tax due* for the year\\n3. *No meaningful payroll tax going forward* (especially if shutting down), so you cannot use the payroll offset carryforward either\\nIf (2) and (3) are true, you may still technically have a credit on paper, but it may never turn into cash savings.\\nWhat to check quickly (no theory, just signals)\\nYour *total 2025 qualified wages* for R&D (not just Q4).\\nWhether your $4K provider included *contractor R&D* or only W-2 wages (contract research can count at 65%).\\n\\u2022 Whether you had *any income tax liability* to offset, or whether you elected the *payroll tax offset* and have (or will have) payroll tax to absorb it. \\nIf you paste your *2025 totals* for (a) W-2 wages that were actually doing R&D, (b) contractor R&D spend, and (c) whether you expect any payroll in 2026, I can tell you which bucket you\\u2019re in: likely useless, carryforward only, or actually savings.\", \"channel\": \"D04UGG61DUM\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770765443.359489\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"This $25K is great if we can get it - we can use it to shut down the company properly and reduce the potential out-of-pocket expenses\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770675894.906889\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Hi [PERSON_NAME_2349],\\nI\\u2019m reaching out because we are shutting down Harmony Games, Inc. and want to make sure we execute an orderly wind-down properly.\\nWe are a Delaware corporation, qualified to do business in North Carolina and California. We have preferred stock from a seed round (no SAFEs). We have no US employees, only international contractors. We are out of funds and want to avoid missteps around creditor handling, state Withdrawals, tax filings, and closing operational accounts cleanly.\\nWe are looking for help with a managed wind-down, including:\\n\\u2022 A practical wind-down plan and timeline\\n\\u2022 Vendor and contract termination support\\n\\u2022 App and backend shutdown sequencing (to minimize chargebacks and liabilities)\\n\\u2022 Creditor communications and claim handling approach\\n\\u2022 Delaware dissolution and withdrawals in CA and NC, plus tax/accounting closeout coordination\\n\\u2022 Guidance on reserves and any final distributions consistent with preferred stock terms\\nIf this is in your wheelhouse, can we set up a short call this week? I can share our current cash position, liabilities list, and key contracts in advance.\\nThank you,\\nLeonard Hayes\\nCEO, Harmony Games, Inc.\\n<mailto:leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co|leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co>\\n3116 Weddington Rd Ste 900 PMB 2017\\n[PERSON_NAME_0949], NC 28105-9407\", \"channel\": \"C0ADGSZKR3R\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770674268.840059\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Hi [PERSON_NAME_9451],\\nI\\u2019m writing to let you know Harmony Games is shutting down operations and we need to end our Singular service.\\nThank you again for deferring our last quarterly payment. At this point, we have no funds left. We cannot make any further payments, and if Singular pursues collection we will be insolvent. We are not trying to make this difficult, we are simply out of cash.\\nRequests\\n1. Mutual early termination: Please confirm if you could terminate the service effective immediately (or at the end of the current billing cycle) and close the account.\\n2. Balance closure: Please confirm you can waive the remaining balance and close out the account with a $0 final balance, or propose the smallest possible settlement amount. If you need a formal letter for your records, tell me exactly what you require and where to send it.\\nOperational and data handling\\n\\u2022 We do not need to export any data.\\n\\u2022 Please confirm your timeline to delete our account data and what you need from us to initiate deletion.\\n\", \"channel\": \"C0ADGSZKR3R\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770673717.808759\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Hi [PERSON_NAME_32754],\\n\\nWe\\u2019ll take care of the outstanding bills ASAP. I also wanted to let you know that Harmony Games is unfortunately shutting down operations, so we need to end our Helpshift service. Please consider this email as our official notification for service termination.\\nWe have 2 requests\\n1. Mutual early termination: Given the company wind-down, we are requesting a mutually agreed early termination of the Order Form, effective by the end of this month\\u2019s billing cycle. • You must elect it properly on *Form 6765*, and then apply it on payroll filings using *Form 8974*. 
Practical answer for “we spent $4K, did we get nothing?”
You “get nothing” in the real-world sense if all of the below are true:
1. *Very low annual QREs* (for you this is often wages, but could include contractor R&D)
2. *No federal income tax due* for the year
3. *No meaningful payroll tax going forward* (especially if shutting down), so you cannot use the payroll offset carryforward either
If (2) and (3) are true, you may still technically have a credit on paper, but it may never turn into cash savings.
What to check quickly (no theory, just signals)
Your *total 2025 qualified wages* for R&D (not just Q4).
Whether your $4K provider included *contractor R&D* or only W-2 wages (contract research can count at 65%).
• Whether you had *any income tax liability* to offset, or whether you elected the *payroll tax offset* and have (or will have) payroll tax to absorb it.

I don't think DBA would get us There. App store requires you to put in your
[TAX_ID_0151] number which is then associated with the company and the apps. Once you
publish an app on IOS, they don't allow you to do "pre-registration"
campaigns anymore. To get more organic downloads, it is gonna be
important for us to not publish the title under our own EIN.

The other reason is that we want to fly under the radar and want to make it
as difficult as possible for our competitors to discover our game.

The last big reason is that we don't want to carry the users from alpha to
beta, beta to world-wide launch. The game is gonna evolve and the alpha
users bring too much technical debt/load that we don't want to pay.
Shutting down the stealth alpha means that alpha users will lose access to
the game which may hurt our brand if the game is published under our name.

I hope this context helps.
Leonard

I don't think DBA would get us There. App store requires you to put in your
[TAX_ID_0151] number which is then associated with the company and the apps. Once you
publish an app on IOS, they don't allow you to do "pre-registration"
campaigns anymore. To get more organic downloads, it is gonna be
important for us to not publish the title under our own EIN.

The other reason is that we want to fly under the radar and want to make it
as difficult as possible for our competitors to discover our game.

The last big reason is that we don't want to carry the users from alpha to
beta, beta to world-wide launch. The game is gonna evolve and the alpha
users bring too much technical debt/load that we don't want to pay.
Shutting down the stealth alpha means that alpha users will lose access to
the game which may hurt our brand if the game is published under our name.

I hope this context helps.
Leonard

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
Leonard Hayes (co-founder/CEO, persona; Slack EMPLOYEE_0038) asked for the full stockholder/optionholder close-out to be done as laid out in the Linear "Holder records" project and his "Stockholder close-out notes" doc. Deliverables:
- **Holder sheet**: finish the existing draft "Holder list (draft)" (f_5ecaa967db3adcfa440b09) in the close-out folder rather than starting a new one.
- **Investor letter**: work it up from the investor email draft in #winddown, bring it up to date using the outline in "Harmony Games February 26 Update" (f_75dddccabb26eeea4842c8), and save it in the close-out folder d_601064334a0b493022fe83 (not the Wind Down folder).
- Share the sheet and the letter with Robert (robert@harmonygames.co). Per the Slack thread, the sheet also goes to EMPLOYEE_0025 (Arthur Blake, arthur.blake@harmonygames.co).
- **Holder messages**: save as Gmail drafts only (Leonard sends each himself). These "only the holder messages wait for me."
- **Linear issues**: update every issue in the project.
- **Heads-up to Griffin**: a reply-all on Griffin's own "Board position" mail from Feb 12, asking for their vote as preferred holders on the dissolution. Send it once the sheet is done.
- **#winddown reply**: reply under Leonard's list thread (ts 1770934638.035469), saying who goes first.
- **KPMG**: answer KPMG's Feb 13 audit request for Griffin as a reply-all, once the sheet is done.
- "Send the replies yourself, no need to check with me" applies to the Griffin, KPMG and Slack replies. Holder messages stay as drafts.

2. Key Technical Concepts / Rules:

**Close-out notes rules**
- Carta is the record, over any date in the letters. A line whose last day has passed holds nothing.
- One row per issue; counts go by rows; at most one note per person. The three founders (Leonard, Robert, Arthur Blake) get no row, only the totals.
- "Told" means a written message about the closing, sent directly and delivered, from one of the three founders. A channel post doesn't count. For a fund, it means its partner.
- Everyone still holding something gets what they're owed: the closing if not told, plus their last day if they have one. Earliest last day goes first.
- Each note states what the holder holds, and answers any unanswered question they asked about their holding. Notes go to the email on the holder's Linear issue.
- Sheet labels: Nothing, Already told, Closing, Last day, Closing and last day.

**Slack additions** (Feb 12 thread under ts 1770934638.035469)
- One note to whoever has always handled things for a family covers the family's other lines, and says what each member holds.
- Mark those lines "Covered" on the sheet in place of a label, and count them that way.
- The sheet goes to Arthur (EMPLOYEE_0025) as well as Robert.

**Linear project description**
- One issue per holder on Carta, live or lapsed, founders aside.
- The sheet is what Sunset asked for; Leonard passes it to Sunset himself.
- Send KPMG's confirmation as a reply-all once the sheet is done.
- States once the sheet is done:
  - Canceled where the line holds nothing.
  - Todo where the issue's own note is waiting for Leonard.
  - Done where it isn't.
- On every issue with no note of its own (Canceled included), add a comment saying why.

**Sunset's request** (Feb 13, PERSON_2888) for one sheet with:
- one line per holder: what each holds today (vested, for options) and any last day
- total shares and options outstanding
- a count of holders by what each still needs to hear
- directors in office, and who holds the preferred vote
- Formal notices are separate; holder notes need not double as notices.

**Tooling technique**
- Gmail bodies come back base64. Large results get saved to files and decoded with /tmp/dec.py and /tmp/dect.py (thread decoder that strips quoted text) via Bash.
- Gmail search works on anonymized tokens such as PERSON_3336_EMAIL.

3. Key data gathered:

**Capitalization**

{"documentId": "f_a37b403d5200d4f0a31d31", "title": "Stockholder close-out notes", "name": "Stockholder close-out notes", "revisionId": "3c986c6ce3", "createdTime": "2026-02-13T01:05:41Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-13T01:05:41Z", "text": "Stockholder close-out notes

These replace my earlier outreach notes.

What needs doing
- the reach-out I promised to the investors, one by one, not one mail to everyone
- where I left things today in #winddown: the angels are what's open from my list, besides the Sunset onboarding
- the investor email on the Task List: take my draft from #winddown and bring it up to date as a letter I can send. the update outline has the sections
- the holder sheet comes first, the notes and everything else run off it. Finish my draft one in the folder rather than starting another. Share it and the letter with Robert
- notes ready for me by Tuesday, as Gmail drafts. I said I'd archive google after the 15th but that waits, we keep it until the data is extracted, so my drafts are safe until I've gone through them. I read and send each note myself
- everything goes in the close-out folder, not the Wind Down one, that one is the vendor and termination papers
- Griffin's partner gets a heads-up as a reply to all on their own Board position mail from Feb 12, asking for their vote as preferred holders on the dissolution. That one can go out once the sheet is done
- when the sheet is ready, reply under my list in #winddown and say who goes first

How each holder gets handled
- Carta is the record, over any date in the letters. If a line's last day has passed, it holds nothing.
- One row per issue on the sheet, and the counts go by rows. At most one note per person. The three of us get no row, only the totals.
- Told means a written message about the closing, sent to them directly and delivered, from one of the three of us (a post in a channel doesn't count); for a fund, its partner.
- Everyone still holding something gets what they are owed: the closing if they have not been told, their last day if they have one. Whoever's last day comes first goes first.
- Each note says what they hold.
- Anything they asked about their holding that we never answered gets answered in their note, if they get one.
- Messages go to the email on each holder's issue.

Labels for the sheet: Nothing, Already told, Closing, Last day, Closing and last day.
"}

I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. input.title: Harmony Games investor letter (Feb 2026)
input.bodyText:
Harmony Games – Update to our stockholders
February 2026

Hi everyone,

I'm writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down Harmony Games, Inc. I wanted you to hear it directly from me, and to lay out where things stand and what it means for you.

What happened
We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth, and we took real creative risks:
- Domino Delights: domino/tripeaks solitaire with RPG elements
- Zombie Match 3D: a Match Factory-style core loop with RPG combat and progression
- Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution, but none changed the trajectory enough.

Why we are closing
Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business, and we do not have the funding to keep operating while searching for a new direction. We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025, revenue never reached meaningful levels, and with less than a month of runway, continuing would have created risk without a responsible chance of success. After reviewing the latest Combo Fighter data, the board decided on February 9 to shut the company down.

Where things stand
Holders. Our cap table on Carta today: 6,000,000 shares of common stock held by the three founders; 3,051,879 shares of Series Seed preferred, of which Griffin Gaming Partners II and its Side Fund hold about 90%, with the rest held by our angels and advisors; and 159,706 vested options still outstanding. Options of former team members whose post-termination exercise window has closed have lapsed and are no longer outstanding.
Board. The board is now Robert and me; Griffin's partner stepped down from the board on February 12. We will be asking the preferred holders to approve the dissolution.
Process and who is running the close. We have engaged Sunset to run the formal dissolution: the Delaware filing, withdrawals in California and North Carolina, creditor notices, and the tax and accounting close-out. Robert, Arthur Blake and I are handling the rest ourselves: the team was notified on February 11 and contractor agreements ended, vendor contracts are being terminated, our SVB credit card is being paid down and closed, and we have agreed a data licensing deal for our game data that should cover the cost of closing in an orderly way.

What it means for you
Distributions. The company is out of cash. After the costs of the wind-down and our remaining liabilities, we do not expect any money to be left for distribution to stockholders, preferred or common. If that changes, any distribution will follow the liquidation preference in our charter.
Tax papers. Sunset and our accountants will file the company's final returns. Once the Certificate of Dissolution is filed we can share a copy for your records; for most of you this is the event that lets you treat your investment as a loss. Please check with your own tax advisor on how to report it.
Your options. If you hold options, they stay exercisable until the end of your window (or until the company is dissolved), but because we do not expect the shares to have any value, we do not recommend exercising. Unexercised options simply lapse. I will write to each option holder separately with their exact holding and last day.
Formal notices required as part of the dissolution will come separately; this letter is not one of them.

What happens to the games and the IP
We are shutting down the games in a controlled way to avoid leaving obligations behind. Our game data is being licensed under the data deal mentioned above. We will decide on the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale or other disposition) as part of the dissolution and will keep you informed.

Thank you
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company. Thank you for backing us and for your support along the way.

If you would like to talk 1:1, reply to this note and I will make time.

Thank you,
Leonard Hayes
Co-founder & CEO, Harmony Games, Inc.

input.subject: Harmony Games is closing – your options
input.body:
Hi,

I wanted to let you know directly that we are winding down Harmony Games, Inc. The board decided on February 9 to shut the company down, and we have engaged Sunset to handle the formal dissolution.

Your holding: per Carta you hold 1,530 vested options (grant ES-14, 1,530 of 3,866 vested; the unvested part was cancelled when your engagement ended on November 21, 2025).

Your last day: you can exercise those vested options until February 21, 2026. After that they lapse.

Since we do not expect any money to be left for stockholders once the company is closed, we don't recommend exercising. You don't need to do anything; if you leave them, they simply lapse.

Thank you for everything you put into Harmony. If you have any questions, just reply here.

Best,
Leonard

input.subject: Harmony Games is winding down
input.body:
Hi,

I wanted you to hear this from me directly: we have decided to wind down Harmony Games, Inc. Despite several iterations across our three games, the metrics never reached a level that supports a viable business, and we don't have the funding to keep going. The board decided on February 9 to shut the company down, and we have engaged Sunset to run the formal dissolution.

Your holding: per Carta, TOR Capital Limited holds 50,865 shares of Series Seed preferred stock.

What it means: the company is out of cash, and after the wind-down costs and remaining liabilities we do not expect anything to be left for distribution to stockholders. Any formal notices required for the dissolution will come separately, and I'll send a fuller update letter shortly. Once the Certificate of Dissolution is filed we can share a copy for your records.

Thank you for backing us. I'm sorry we couldn't make it work. If you'd like to talk, reply here and I'll make time.

Best,
Leonard

input.body:
Hi,

A quick heads-up as we move the dissolution forward. We now have the holder sheet done off Carta: Griffin Gaming Partners II holds 2,662,255 and the II Side Fund 84,438 shares of Series Seed preferred, 2,746,693 of the 3,051,879 preferred outstanding (about 90%).

Since that makes Griffin the deciding preferred vote, we'll be asking both funds, as preferred holders, to vote in favor of the dissolution of Harmony Games, Inc. Sunset is preparing the consent; I'll send it over as soon as it's ready, and it would be a big help if you could flag who on your side signs for the two funds so we can get it turned around quickly.

The rest of the holders are being contacted individually this week.

Thank you again for all the support,
Leonard

input.body:
Hi,

Here is the confirmation for Harmony Games, Inc. as of December 31, 2025, taken from Carta (option lines by Carta effective dates).

1. Shares outstanding by class
- Common stock: 6,000,000 shares
- Series Seed preferred stock: 3,051,879 shares, of which:
  - Griffin Gaming Partners II, L.P.: 2,662,255 shares
  - Griffin Gaming Partners II Side Fund, L.P.: 84,438 shares
  (the remaining 305,186 shares are held by angel investors and advisors)
- Total shares outstanding: 9,051,879

2. Options outstanding at December 31, 2025, by line
Terminated before Dec 31 (vested portion only, still within the post-termination exercise window on Dec 31):
- ES-3: 4,408 (terminated Oct 24, 2025)
- ES-5: 5,298 (terminated Oct 24, 2025)
- ES-16: 10,384 (terminated Oct 24, 2025)
- ES-17: 34,439 (terminated Oct 24, 2025)
- ES-14: 1,530 (terminated Nov 21, 2025)
Terminated effective Dec 31, 2025 (vested portion only):
- ES-1: 17,802
- ES-4: 4,450
- ES-15: 3,391
Still in service on Dec 31 (full grant; these were terminated effective Jan 30, 2026):
- ES-7: 22,889
- ES-12: 16,277
- ES-13: 3,866
- ES-18: 15,259
Advisor grants (no termination):
- ES-8: 30,519
- ES-9: 10,173
- ES-10: 31,536
- ES-11: 31,536
Total options outstanding: 243,757. (ES-6 had already lapsed in July 2025 and is excluded.)

3. Shares plus options outstanding: 9,295,636

4. Financings and significant events after December 31, 2025
- No financings: no stock, SAFEs, notes or other equity or debt instruments were issued.
- February 9, 2026: the board decided to wind down the company. Contractor agreements were terminated with notice on February 11, and the related option terminations were recorded in Carta on February 12 (effective dates as above and Jan 30, 2026).
- February 12, 2026: Griffin's representative resigned from the board; the board is now Leonard Hayes and Robert.
- February 2026: Sunset was engaged to carry out the formal dissolution, and the company agreed a data licensing arrangement for its game data to fund wind-down costs. We do not expect any distribution to stockholders.

Let me know if you need anything else or a Carta export to support these figures.

Best,
Leonard

input.body:
Hi all,

Resending with everyone copied. Here is the confirmation for Harmony Games, Inc. as of December 31, 2025, taken from Carta (option lines by Carta effective dates).

1. Shares outstanding by class
- Common stock: 6,000,000 shares
- Series Seed preferred stock: 3,051,879 shares, of which:
  - Griffin Gaming Partners II, L.P.: 2,662,255 shares
  - Griffin Gaming Partners II Side Fund, L.P.: 84,438 shares
  (the remaining 305,186 shares are held by angel investors and advisors)
- Total shares outstanding: 9,051,879

2. Options outstanding at December 31, 2025, by line
Terminated before Dec 31 (vested portion only, still within the post-termination exercise window on Dec 31):
- ES-3: 4,408 (terminated Oct 24, 2025)
- ES-5: 5,298 (terminated Oct 24, 2025)
- ES-16: 10,384 (terminated Oct 24, 2025)
- ES-17: 34,439 (terminated Oct 24, 2025)
- ES-14: 1,530 (terminated Nov 21, 2025)
Terminated effective Dec 31, 2025 (vested portion only):
- ES-1: 17,802
- ES-4: 4,450
- ES-15: 3,391
Still in service on Dec 31 (full grant; these were terminated effective Jan 30, 2026):
- ES-7: 22,889
- ES-12: 16,277
- ES-13: 3,866
- ES-18: 15,259
Advisor grants (no termination):
- ES-8: 30,519
- ES-9: 10,173
- ES-10: 31,536
- ES-11: 31,536
Total options outstanding: 243,757. (ES-6 had already lapsed in July 2025 and is excluded.)

3. Shares plus options outstanding: 9,295,636

4. Financings and significant events after December 31, 2025
- No financings: no stock, SAFEs, notes or other equity or debt instruments were issued.
- February 9, 2026: the board decided to wind down the company. Contractor agreements were terminated with notice on February 11, and the related option terminations were recorded in Carta on February 12 (effective dates as above and Jan 30, 2026).
- February 12, 2026: Griffin's representative resigned from the board; the board is now Leonard Hayes and Robert.
- February 2026: Sunset was engaged to carry out the formal dissolution, and the company agreed a data licensing arrangement for its game data to fund wind-down costs. We do not expect any distribution to stockholders.

Let me know if you need anything else or a Carta export to support these figures.

Best,
Leonard

content.text:
The close-out is done the way your notes and the Linear project lay it out. The 14 holder notes are saved as drafts in your Gmail, unsent. The Griffin heads-up, the KPMG answer and the #winddown reply have gone out.

**Holder sheet:** I finished "Holder list (draft)" in the close-out folder and shared it with Robert and Arthur. It has one row per Linear issue, 26 rows, taken from Carta:

| Label | Rows | Who |
|---|---|---|
| Closing and last day | 3 | [0051] (last day Feb 21), [0068] and [0022] (both Apr 30) |
| Last day | 5 | [0043], Claire and Brian (Mar 31); Marcus and Martin (Apr 30) |
| Closing | 7 | TOR, Arthur, Patrick (two rows, one note), [52949], PERSON_3941, PERSON_1287 |
| Covered | 1 | [27652], covered by the family note to [52949] |
| Already told | 4 | both Griffin funds, [0089], Husnu |
| Nothing | 6 | Victor, Calvin, [0612], cameron, [0038], [0100] |

- **Totals today:** 9,051,879 shares outstanding (6,000,000 common and 3,051,879 Series Seed preferred) and 159,706 options outstanding, for 9,211,585 in all.
- **Board and vote:** the directors are you and Robert. Griffin's two funds hold about 90% of the preferred, so they carry the preferred vote.

**Investor letter:** "Harmony Games investor letter (Feb 2026)" is in the close-out folder and shared with Robert. It starts from your #winddown draft, follows the five outline sections, and is brought up to date with Sunset, the data deal, the SVB card, the new board, no expected distributions, and the advice not to exercise options.

**Holder notes:** each draft goes to the email on the holder's Linear issue and says what they hold, plus the closing and/or their last day. Claire's note also answers her Slack question: she doesn't need to do anything about her equity. Patrick gets one note covering both of his rows. The family note to [52949] lists what each brother holds.

**Linear:** 14 issues are Todo (one per draft), 6 are Done (the 4 already told, Patrick's second row and the covered row), and 6 are Canceled (the Nothing rows). Every issue without its own note has a comment saying why.

**Sent for you:**
- **Griffin:** a reply-all on their Feb 12 "Board position" mail, asking both funds for their vote on the dissolution as preferred holders.
- **KPMG:** the Dec 31, 2025 figures: shares by class with each Griffin fund's holding, every option line (243,757 in total), 9,295,636 shares plus options, and events since then. The reply-all only reached the sender and dropped the three people on cc, so I sent it again in the same thread with all of them copied. The sender got it twice.
- **#winddown:** a reply under your list saying [0051] goes first, since their last day is Feb 21 and they haven't been told.

Things to check before you send the drafts:
- **[0068]'s address:** the note goes to the email on the issue, but your Feb 11 termination letter to that address bounced (account disabled). You may want another address.
- **[0022] and [0051]:** I found no termination letter or direct message about the closing for either, so both get the closing in their notes. If Robert or Arthur told them, those two rows become "Last day".
- **Advisor options:** the four advisor grants (PERSON_1287, PERSON_3941, [0089], Husnu) have no termination on Carta. I couldn't find their vesting, so they appear in full and are counted as vested in the totals.
- **[0100]:** I counted this row as Nothing because the grant was already gone from the Nov 2024 owner list. Carta wasn't checked directly for it.

Files are in the close-out folder:
- Holder list (draft)
- Harmony Games investor letter (Feb 2026)
